subject: treasureChest
reasoning:
I'm planning the treasure chest design: a wooden box body with a curved lid, iron bands, brass corner plates, a lock, handles, and possibly a hinged lid I can pose open to reveal some gold coins inside.

I'll build it mostly from primitive geometries—boxes for the body, cylinders for the bands, spheres for studs—sized around 0.9m wide, 0.55m deep, 0.6m tall, standing at y=0 and facing +Z. For the hinge, I'm working out how to attach a lid geometry to a joint bone positioned at the back top edge so I can pose it to swing open, making sure the geometry's local coordinates line up correctly with the joint so the rotation works as expected.

For the lid's dome shape, I'm considering a half-cylinder made by rotating a CylinderGeometry with a partial theta sweep so it bulges upward, though I'm also weighing whether a sweep-based approach would give cleaner control over the curve.

I'll scale the geometry vertices to flatten the dome height, and simplify by just stacking a box slab for the lid base with the half-cylinder dome on top, defining body dimensions like width, depth, and height for the chest.

Working out the lid pivot: the hinge sits at the back top edge, with the lid geometry centered in z around the joint so the front edge lifts upward when rotating about the x-axis to open.

The lid geometry sits within model coordinates, with the pivot positioned at the hinge point so rotation opens it correctly. I'm also checking how the joint hierarchy roots to the body, making sure the chest or hips joint anchors everything properly.

Now I need to make the chest interior visible once the lid opens—since the body is a solid box, I'll add a dark inset box to represent the opening and layer gold coins or a flattened gold pile on top to simulate treasure inside.

That region stays hidden when closed since the lid remains a solid slab covering it, only revealed on opening. For the coins, I'll scatter small flat cylinders across an elliptical area on the pile, randomizing their positions and stacking heights to create a natural pile effect.

I'll give the coins a gold color, and add a few gem accents using small octahedron shapes in red and blue for variety. For the chest's hardware, I'm planning iron straps as thin dark boxes running across the front and back faces, plus horizontal bands, while being careful to position them so they don't collide with the lock plate centered on the lid's front edge.

Since the lid is posed open, I'll attach the lock plate directly to the lid bone so it moves rigidly with it rather than staying fixed to the body, placing it near the lid's front face using an explicit position offset. I'll also make sure the whole model's feet rest exactly at y=0 so it stands properly on the ground.

Now I'm working out the body's vertical layout with small feet underneath, then figuring out torus-based side handles — rotating the torus geometry so its ring lies in the vertical YZ plane against the end faces rather than lying flat, so the handles face outward correctly.

I'm placing the handles slightly offset from the end faces so they stick out, then adding corner and strap details: vertical brass straps across the front and back faces positioned at the surface depth, skipping the center front strap since that's where the lid lock plate goes instead.

I'm also planning rivet studs as tiny spheres scattered along the straps, and figuring out how to approximate a dome-following strap across the curved lid top using a slightly raised box rather than modeling a true arc.

Still positioning dome pieces...

Scattering coin cylinders across an elliptical footprint with slight height variation and random tilts, using two gold shades for variety, so the pile looks naturally heaped rather than perfectly flat.

For gems, I'll add three stretched octahedrons in red and teal nestled at the top of the pile for a bit of sparkle. So I should explicitly specify bones everywhere rather than rely on nearest-joint inference — root joint named "body" for all body parts (base, straps, feet), and the "lid" joint for lid parts. For each handle, I'm rotating the torus so its ring lies in the side plane, then adding small mounting plates where the ring meets the chest at top and bottom. I'm also placing a lock plate on the lid's front face just below the lid's top edge, centered horizontally.

Then I'm defining a hinge knuckle cylinder rotated to run along the X-axis at the lid's back joint, attached to the body with brass hinge bands on the lid side.

Finalizing the metal and wood palette with iron, brass, and two wood tones, keeping within a 64-color flat palette, and deciding to use the library's grain paint function on the body and lid boxes to simulate wood planking by streaking along the X-axis, possibly extending grain to the dome as well, while keeping metal parts flat-colored and using cylinders with 8-12 sides for detail before moving on to shaping small octahedron gems.

Working through gem colors, coin arrangement using a seeded rng, and the module's import and meta export structure, then verifying the pose API signature and confirming the lid's rest pose works for an open chest.
